newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes down, silver up on world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes down, silver up on world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees lower at 4,590 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,600 rupees amid sluggish physical buying while a weak trend in the world market dragged local prices lower after a steady start.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 53,700 rupees per piece against the previous close of 53,800 rupees.

** Silver (.999) closed steady at 6,750 rupees per kg against the previous close but up 25 rupees against the opening level of 6,725 rupees as reports of a recovery in world prices helped local markets bounce back after a lower start. Silver was up by 15 rupees per kg on Tuesday.

Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees lower at 4,590 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,600 rupees as a weak trend in world markets prompted fresh selling during the day after a steady trend in early trade, dealers said.
Sluggish physical enquiries kept market sentiment subdued and volume was at a low ebb.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 53,700 rupees per piece against the previous close of 53,800 rupees on fresh selling.

Silver (.999) closed steady at 6,750 rupees per kg against the previous close but up 25 rupees against the opening level of 6,725 rupees per kg as reports of a fresh recovery in world prices dragged local prices upward after an easy start. Silver was up 15 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
"Limited arrivals also helped local prices to trim early losses towards the close but demand from the industrial buyers remained dull during the day," said Mahavir Shah, a leading dealer.
